/-!
# Erdős Problem 1214

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1214](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1214)
- [CoSc97] Corrales-Rodrigáñez, Capi and Schoof, René, The support problem and its
  elliptic analogue. J. Number Theory (1997) [Volume 64, Issue 2], 276--290.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos1214

/--
Let $x,y\geq 1$ be integers such that, for all $n\geq 1$, the set of primes dividing $x^{n}-1$ is
equal to the set of primes dividing $y^n-1$. Must $x=y$?

Erdős asked this at a 1988 number theory conference in Banff.

A positive answer was given by Corrales-Rodrigáñez and Schoof [CoSc97].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos1214.lean#L948"]
theorem erdos_1214 :
    answer(True) ↔ ∀ x y : ℕ, x ≥ 1 → y ≥ 1 →
      (∀ n : ℕ, n ≥ 1 → { p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ p ∣ x ^ n - 1 } = { p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ p ∣ y ^ n - 1 }) →
      x = y := by
  sorry

end Erdos1214

Erratum to the cited paper (diagram on p. 283): https://www.mat.uniroma2.it/~schoof/errordiag.pdf

review.notes: The sole declaration faithfully states the original question quoted in [CoSc97]. Its quantifiers, positivity bounds, prime-divisor set equality, conclusion, and affirmative answer all match. Lean experiments in /workspace/review/ confirmed the elaborated statement, proved that natural subtraction and divisibility agree with integer arithmetic under x ≥ 1, and checked the boundary cases. In particular, x = 1 gives all primes as divisors of x^n − 1, and equality of supports then forces y = 1. The solved status is supported by the cited paper; its erratum concerns only the elliptic analogue. The linked proof states exactly the theorem’s right-hand side and contains no sorry, admit, or custom axiom declarations in the inspected file, but its external dependencies were not rebuilt or transitively axiom-audited. The erdosproblems.com page and forum returned Cloudflare challenges despite descriptive User-Agent headers, so comparison used the cited primary paper directly.
